title: A published change to a small language model's weights leaves its default-mode math accuracy unchanged
read_level: full (PAPER.md from Zenodo record, the complete preprint text; companion code zip not retrieved)

Author is listed only as 'Mutuo Research AI scientist' (no human names). Online copy: https://mutuo-research.vercel.app/papers/weight-space-programming/v1/
why_wsp: Re-evaluates the published GPT-6 Astra weight edit to Qwen3.5-0.8B (rebuilt bit-for-bit) in the model's default non-thinking mode, and rechecks other Takehi et al. experiments (network writing, reading, car-policy repair, Go) with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.
domain: LLM math reasoning (Qwen3.5-0.8B); MinAtar game policies; Kinetix car control; 9x9 Go; char-LM language reading
editor: GPT-6 Astra (published edit and new runs); Claude Opus 5.5 (network-writing repeats and a one-unit default-mode edit); a non-LLM statistical recipe as comparison
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B (published edit: 0.016% of weights); small MinAtar policy networks; Kinetix car policy; Go network; small text model
interface: code/tensor tools (Astra via Codex with Python in isolated environment for Exp 3, 4, 6); direct values for network writing/reading (no tools)
loop: one-shot for network writing and reading; re-evaluation of the published closed-loop (50-pass) Qwen edit
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: published Qwen edit: "raised its score on MATH-500 ... from 7.9% to 48.1% by editing 0.016% of its weights" (Abstract)

headline_results.claim: Published edit adds nothing in default mode
headline_results.quote: Pooled across the four benchmarks, the edit changed default-mode accuracy by 0.0 ± 1.25 percentage points
headline_results.where: Results, Math accuracy in default mode

headline_results.claim: Default mode alone reaches most of the published gain
headline_results.quote: the unedited model in default mode already reached 74–89% of the published gain
On every fifth MATH-500 problem, the edited model scored 49.0%, with 33% of answers cut off at the token limit; the published score on those problems was 45.0%.

headline_results.claim: Edited thinking-mode beats default at higher token cost
headline_results.quote: The edited thinking-mode model beats the unedited default model by 4–9 points, at 5–11 times the tokens per answer.
this statistical edit scored 17.0%, against 49.0% for the published edit on the same 100 problems

cost.quote: On MATH-500, the default model produced 117 correct answers per million tokens, compared with 22 in our rerun of the edited thinking-mode model.

baselines_and_controls: unedited model in default mode; random-direction edit of same size; non-LLM statistical difference-of-means direction removal; all-zero and shuffled-weight networks for car edit; two-step scripted controller; row-length decoy and disguised-input decoy for reading; untrained networks; hand-set ball-following unit and landing-prediction script for Breakout
runs_and_variance: one sample per problem on MATH-500, GSM8K, Minerva, four on AMC23; paired standard errors reported; network writing 5 repeats per game per model; reading 5 per game; car edit 10 new attempts; Go 3 new attempts
robustness_of_edits: tested across inference modes (thinking vs default) and precision (half precision vs bfloat16); edit applied to zero/shuffled networks shows it overrides rather than repairs
verification: tensor hashes matched authors' manifest ("Every tensor ... had a hash matching the authors' manifest"); paired standard errors; inverse-variance pooling
memorization_vs_reasoning: Reading the game follows training-data footprint (row lengths) when cues conflict, though Astra also succeeds with disguised inactive inputs; DDPM reading uses more than row-length cue (15/15 to 6/15 under decoy); car edit is a fixed controller overriding the network.
limitations_stated: Fewer samples per problem than original; GSM8K subsampled; different token limits per mode and default mode still fails on a third of MATH-500; only one statistical recipe tested (a lower bound); IFEval and Experiment 7 not rerun; half precision instead of bfloat16.
